query_data – SQL Analysis

src/query_data.py

Answer the assignment’s analysis questions with raw SQL.

This module is part of the database layer. It connects to PostgreSQL with psycopg, runs one query per assignment question against the applicants table (created by load_data), and prints the answers.

The database is chosen by the DATABASE_URL environment variable. If it isn’t set, the libpq variables PGDATABASE (default gradcafe_applications), PGUSER (default postgres), PGPASSWORD, PGHOST (default localhost) and PGPORT (default 5432) are used.

Example:

python query_data.py

All work happens inside main(), so importing this module (e.g. from Sphinx autodoc or pytest) does not open a database connection.

query_data.libpq_url(url)[source]

Convert a SQLAlchemy-style URL into one psycopg/libpq accepts.

Parameters:

url (str) – e.g. postgresql+psycopg://u:p@host:5432/db.

Returns:

e.g. postgresql://u:p@host:5432/db.

Return type:

str

>>> libpq_url("postgresql+psycopg://u:p@h/db")
'postgresql://u:p@h/db'
query_data.get_connection()[source]

Open a PostgreSQL connection from DATABASE_URL or the PG* variables.

Returns:

An open psycopg connection. The caller must close it.

Return type:

psycopg.Connection

Raises:

psycopg.OperationalError – If the database is unreachable.

query_data.run_queries(conn)[source]

Run every analysis query and return the raw answers.

Parameters:

conn (psycopg.Connection) – An open psycopg connection.

Returns:

A dict with keys count1, percent_international, avg_gpa, avg_gre_q, avg_gre_v, avg_gre_aw, avg_gpa_american_fall2026, fall_2025_acceptance_pct, avg_gpa_accepted_fall2026, jhu_ms_cs_count, original_field_count, llm_field_count, gpa_bucket_rows (list of (bucket, total, pct)) and term_count_rows (list of (term, count)).

Return type:

dict

query_data.term_trend(term_count_rows)[source]

Describe the trend in applicant counts from the first to last term.

Parameters:

term_count_rows (list) – (term, count) rows in chronological order.

Returns:

"Trending up", "Trending down" or "No trend".

Return type:

str

>>> term_trend([("Fall 2024", 10), ("Fall 2025", 20)])
'Trending up'
query_data.print_results(r)[source]

Print every question and its answer to stdout.

Parameters:

r (dict) – The dict returned by run_queries().

Return type:

None

query_data.main()[source]

Command-line entry point: connect, run all queries, print answers.

The connection is always closed, even if a query fails.

Return type:

None
